text.p: Norwegian airline company Braathens SAFE said on Monday it had formed a strategic alliance with KLM Royal Dutch Airline.
Braathens SAFE said that as part of the agreement, KLM had agreed, in principle, to buy a 30 percent stake in Braathens.
Braathens said financial terms of the acquisition had not yet been settled.

"Braathens SAFE and KLM expect that the close partnership will substantially strengthen the European market position and customer preference both for the Norwegian carrier and for KLM and its partners," Braathens said in a statement.
"Braathens' strong regional position coupled with the international network of KLM and its partners will strengthen the group's European market position."
Both transactions have been submitted to relevant regulatory authorities for review. Braathens said the parties hoped to enter a final agreement within four to eight weeks.

The Oslo-based airline said the partnership would be implemented in phases and would include greater coordination of connecting services and offer a wide selection of connecting services through Amsterdam's Schiphol airport using the KLM partners network.
The two airlines are considering increasing the frequency of services between Norway and Schipol and intensifying cooperation between Braathens and AirUK on Norway-United Kingdom routes.
KLM and its alliance partner, Northwest Airlines, will focus on creating optimal connections between Scandinavian markets and the United States.
Braathens and KLM will also join forces in marketing and sales and examine potential for cooperation in areas such as equipment, technical maintenance and purchasing.
They will also link Braathens' frequent flier programme, BRACard, and KLM's Flying Dutchman programme.
